items.title: Wilson "Willie T" Turbinton Interview, 1990-09
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Brad, do you have anything else you want to add?

ctx.x: Well, not really. I mean, I'm sure that when I leave here, I'll probably say, well, that was something else that I could have said. I just hope that through your efforts of bringing this to people's attention, that maybe they will see reason to start plugging into people who are innovators of the music, and may have some different suggestions as to how to make it more appealing to younger players that might want to pursue a higher form of the music, not for their music to be dictated to and suppressed by record…
Brad, do you have anything else you want to add? Hello? Hello?

A slowish but enormously graceful interpretation of the second movement is followed by a finale of such manically driven yet completely controlled ferocity that for once it is not the sonata's famous opening movement, which remains most clearly in the mind.
